title: JavaScript collections versus C# List and Dictionary
hook: C# collections are generic, strongly typed, and live on the CLR heap with predictable semantics. JavaScript Array, Map, and Set are dynamic, duck-typed, and power the same patterns — but with holes, SameValueZero, and prototype methods instead of LINQ extension methods.

blocks.text: **Array** ≈ **List<T>** (dynamic) but untyped and sparse-capable. **Map** ≈ **Dictionary<TKey,TValue>**. **Set** ≈ **HashSet<T>**. **WeakMap** ≈ **ConditionalWeakTable**. JS has no **List<T>** separate from Array. LINQ lives on **IEnumerable**; JS uses **Array.prototype** methods and iterables. Index access on JS Array is always number-coerced string key.

entries.plainDefinition: Dynamic array with typed elements and Capacity.
Hash map with typed keys — throws on duplicate Add.
C# deferred/eager query operators on IEnumerable.
map, filter, reduce — eager on JS Array.

blocks.text: Developers switching stacks reach for familiar patterns — knowing Map vs Dictionary and when JS Array holes matter prevents porting bugs. LINQ deferred execution differs from chained JS array methods which are eager.

blocks.title: Translation cheat sheet
blocks.body: List → Array. Dictionary → Map. HashSet → Set. foreach → for...of. LINQ Where → filter. Select → map.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Typed storage
items.body: C# compiler enforces T; JS validate at boundary.

items.title: Key types
items.body: Dictionary needs GetHashCode; Map uses SameValueZero.

items.title: Queries
items.body: LINQ deferred until GetEnumerator; JS filter/map build new array immediately.

items.title: Nullability
items.body: C# NRT on references; JS null/undefined both possible.

snippet.label: JS filter/map chain
snippet.explanation: Eager — each method allocates new array. Equivalent to LINQ Where then Select.ToList().

snippet.label: C# LINQ equivalent
snippet.explanation: LINQ can defer until enumeration unless ToList materializes — JS chain always materializes intermediate arrays unless using iterators/generators.

snippet.label: Map vs Dictionary keys
snippet.explanation: JS Map accepts NaN; C# Dictionary rejects NaN as key — porting gotcha.

snippet.label: Grouping pattern
snippet.explanation: reduce builds record of arrays — common JS pattern; C# GroupBy returns IGrouping sequence.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Assuming JS Array same as fixed C# array T[n]. Using object {} as Dictionary with object keys. Expecting LINQ deferred semantics from filter(). Ignoring NaN key difference. Not validating types after JSON.parse when porting C# DTO code.

blocks.text: **IEnumerable deferral** vs **JS eager arrays** — use generators or iterator helpers for lazy LINQ-like chains. **Span<T>** and **Memory<T>** have no JS equivalent — typed arrays closest for binary. **Concurrent collections** in .NET vs single-threaded JS — use Workers for parallel. **Equality**: C# IEquatable vs JS SameValueZero. Know **Array.sort** mutates; LINQ OrderBy returns new sequence.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Maps List to fixed array T[n]. Cannot translate GroupBy to reduce. Says LINQ and filter both lazy.

interviewTakeaways: Array ≈ List — untyped, sparse possible, prototype methods.
Map ≈ Dictionary; Set ≈ HashSet; WeakMap ≈ ConditionalWeakTable.
filter/map eager; LINQ often deferred until enumerate.
60s: Translation table. NaN Map key. Validate JSON. Lazy JS via generators. sort mutates.

Strong: "NaN as Map key works; C# Dictionary throws — porting detail."
